newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended strong on Tuesday, with prices marked up against stronger Bund futures but cash trade on hold until the results of this afternoon's FOMC meeting are known, dealers said.
"The action will be at the open tomorrow, today was a snorer," one said. The U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to announce its decision on interest rates around 1915 GMT.
Anticipation of a moderate, 25 basis point, rise in U.S. interest rates was widespread, with most players judging that a small tightening would have very little impact.

One dealer, however, said a 25 basis point rise would still see the market losing ground as it would not remove the spectre of another short-term tightening. A 0.5 percent hike would shake out all uncertainty and get the market going up, he said.

There had been some light dealing through the session, largely in the mid curve area, as players squared positions ahead of the announcement and institutional investors traded the curve, a broker said.
Business was concentrated in the 2000 and 2003 maturities, he said, and there had been some switching with Germany in the same area.
Spreads against Bunds remained largely stable through the day, with the Guilder curve flattening a little later. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
